tools.name: get_postal_code
tools.description:
Postal code with all its settlements.

Everything about one postal code: its state, its municipality and every settlement in it
(colonias, fraccionamientos, barrios...). Use it to fill an address form as soon as the user
types their postal code.

Returns every settlement (not paginated; the largest postal code has 291). Optional blocks with
`include`: `location` (reference point), `metro` (metropolitan area) and `sat` (SAT keys for
CFDI 4.0) on paid plans; the demo postal codes return the three
blocks on every plan. A postal code that does not exist returns 404
`/errors/postal-code-not-found`, which does not count toward your quota.

With `as_of` you get the postal code as SEPOMEX had it on a past date: its settlements on that
day, from the most recent SEPOMEX file of that date or earlier (`as_of.sepomex_date`). Useful to
check an address that was captured or invoiced back then. Dates go from `history_since` (see
/v1/meta) to today; earlier dates return 400 `/errors/as-of-out-of-range`, because there is no
record of what the catalog said before. A postal code that did not exist on that date returns
404. `include` cannot be combined with `as_of`.

**Plan:** every plan.

fields.description: Top-level fields to return. Allowed: postal_code, state, municipality, office, settlement_count, settlements, data_version, sat (with include=sat), location (with include=location), metro_area (with include=metro) and as_of (with as_of).

include.description: Optional blocks to add (`sat,location,metro`). `sat`: SAT data for CFDI 4.0; requires a paid plan. `location`: reference location of the postal code; requires a paid plan. `metro`: metropolitan area of the postal code; requires a paid plan. The demo postal codes in /v1/postal-codes/{code} return the three blocks on every plan.

as_of.description: Date (YYYY-MM-DD) to get the postal code as SEPOMEX had it that day, from `history_since` (see /v1/meta) to today in Mexico City. Cannot be combined with `include`.

annotations.title: Postal code with all its settlements

tools.name: get_postal_code_history
tools.description:
Change history of a postal code.

What happened to a postal code over time: settlements that were added, removed or renamed,
and settlements that moved to or from it. Useful when an address you stored no longer validates.

Every recorded change of the postal code and of its settlements, oldest first. Also works for
postal codes that no longer exist, as long as they existed after `history_since` (see
/v1/meta). An empty `data` means no changes since `history_since`. Not paginated.

With `include=sat` it also has the changes of the postal code and its settlements in the SAT
catalog (`sat_postal_code`, `sat_settlement`) since `sat_history_since`, merged in order:
when the SAT changed a key, the border incentive or the time zone of the postal code, or added,
removed or renamed one of its settlements (`c_Colonia`).

**Plan:** every plan; `include=sat`, paid plans (Basic and higher), and the demo postal codes on
every plan.

include.description: `sat`: also the changes in the SAT catalog (paid plans: Basic and higher; the demo postal codes on every plan).

annotations.title: Change history of a postal code

tools.name: batch_get_postal_codes
tools.description:
Batch lookup of postal codes.

Look up many postal codes at once; for example, to check every address in your customer
list.

Up to 100 postal codes per request (`codes`, comma-separated), with the same `include` blocks as
/v1/postal-codes/{code}. One item per requested code, in the same order, with `found` and
either the same `result` as /v1/postal-codes/{code} or the `error` of that code: one bad code
never fails the whole batch. Counts as one request per code.

**Plan:** Business and Enterprise.

include.description: Optional blocks to add (`sat,location,metro`). `sat`: SAT data for CFDI 4.0; requires a paid plan. `location`: reference location of the postal code; requires a paid plan. `metro`: metropolitan area of the postal code; requires a paid plan. The demo postal codes in /v1/postal-codes/{code} return the three blocks on every plan.

tools.name: validate_postal_code_settlement
tools.description:
Validate that a settlement belongs to a postal code.

Check that the settlement (colonia) your user typed really belongs to the postal code, before you save the address, ship or invoice.

Tolerates case, accents, common abbreviations, the settlement type at the beginning, spaces, articles and the rest of the address at the end (municipality, state, "C.P."), but never corrects silently: only an exact or equivalent name is `valid`; anything else is a suggestion with its `confidence` and `reason`. Numbers must have the same value: "Sección 2" and "Sección II" are different settlements.

`outcome` gives the conclusion: `valid`; `ambiguous` (several settlements of the postal code have that name: choose one from `same_name_settlements`); `approximate` (see `suggestions`); `other_postal_code` (the name exists in another postal code of the municipality or state, in `found_in_other_postal_codes`); `not_found`; `postal_code_not_found`; and, with `include=sat` or `include=cfdi`, `sat_only` (only the SAT has it there; its key can be used in a CFDI). When SEPOMEX renamed, moved or removed a settlement with that name in the postal code, `history` says where it is today.

`include=sat` adds whether the settlement has a SAT key (`c_Colonia`), with the conclusion in `sat.status`; `include=cfdi` adds the `Domicilio` node of Carta Porte 3.1 and Comercio Exterior 2.0 with the SAT keys, each attribute with its `status`.

**Plan:** every plan; `include=sat` and `include=cfdi`, paid plans (Basic and higher).

The full description and every response field: call get_colonix_guide with topic `validate_postal_code_settlement`.

settlement.description: Settlement name as typed by the user (2 to 100 characters, up to 12 words).

include.description: Extra blocks (paid plans: Basic and higher): `sat`, whether the settlement has a SAT key for CFDI 4.0; `cfdi`, the `Domicilio` node of the CFDI complements (Carta Porte, Comercio Exterior) with the SAT keys.

annotations.title: Validate that a settlement belongs to a postal code

tools.name: list_postal_codes
tools.description:
List postal codes.

Find postal codes by area: every postal code of a city, a municipality or a state, or the
ones that start with some digits.

Filter by `prefix`, `state`, `municipality` or `city`. Ordered by postal code. Paginated: follow
`next_cursor` to get every result (e.g. the 172 postal codes of the city of Guadalajara fit in one
page with `limit=500`).

**Plan:** every plan.

Returns one page. If `next_cursor` is not null and the user needs more results, call again with `cursor` set to it; never walk every page to copy the catalog.

prefix.description: First 1 to 5 digits of the postal code.

city.description: City name as SEPOMEX writes it ("Ciudad de México", not "CDMX"), ignoring case and accents; a name that does not match returns no results.

limit.description: Page size (1–500, default 50). There is no "unlimited" value: to get every result, follow `next_cursor` until it is null.

cursor.description: Opaque value of `next_cursor` from the previous page, sent as is. Only valid for the data version that issued it (otherwise 400 /errors/cursor-expired).

tools.name: search_settlements
tools.description:
Search settlements.

Search settlements by name, postal code, state or city; for example, to find the postal code of
a colonia when the user only knows its name.

Requires at least one of `q`, `postal_code`, `state` or `city`. Ordered by postal code and name.
Paginated: follow `next_cursor` to get every result (e.g. the 434 settlements of the city of
Guadalajara fit in one page with `limit=500`).

**Plan:** every plan.

Returns one page. If `next_cursor` is not null and the user needs more results, call again with `cursor` set to it; never walk every page to copy the catalog.

q.description: Text to search, ignoring case and accents (2 to 100 characters, up to 12 words).

city.description: City name as SEPOMEX writes it ("Ciudad de México", not "CDMX"), ignoring case and accents; a name that does not match returns no results.

zone.description: Zone. The catalog values (urbano, semiurbano) are also accepted.

fuzzy.description: Tolerate typos in `q` (one per word of 4 to 7 letters, two in longer words; words of 3 letters or less must be exact). Each result then says `match`: exact or approximate.

limit.description: Page size (1–500, default 50). There is no "unlimited" value: to get every result, follow `next_cursor` until it is null.

cursor.description: Opaque value of `next_cursor` from the previous page, sent as is. Only valid for the data version that issued it (otherwise 400 /errors/cursor-expired).

tools.name: autocomplete_settlements
tools.description:
Address autocomplete.

Suggest settlements while your user types, even with typos, so they pick the right one
instead of writing it.

`q` is read like the validation reads a settlement name: common abbreviations ("col", "nte",
"fracc", "sta"), the settlement type at the beginning ("colonia roma norte") and an ordinal in
any form ("3a", "3ra", "tercera" and "III") are understood. If `q` is only digits, suggests by
postal code prefix; digits together with words ("06700 roma") keep the settlements of the
postal codes that start with those digits.

Order: first the urban settlements of the largest metropolitan areas (by number of
settlements; central municipalities before exterior ones), and within each size the exact
name, then names starting with `q`, then the rest, shorter names first. Settlement types that
are not housing (Equipamiento, Aeropuerto, Zona industrial, militar, naval, federal or
comercial, Puerto, Campamento) come last. Filter by `state` and `municipality` to suggest only
around your user. Not paginated: returns the best `limit` suggestions. With `fuzzy=true`,
suggestions with typos come after the exact ones. Call it from your server and wait for a
short pause in the typing (debounce): every request counts.

**Plan:** every plan.

q.description: Text typed by the user (2 to 100 characters, up to 12 words).

fuzzy.description: Tolerate typos in `q` (one per word of 4 to 7 letters, two in longer words; words of 3 letters or less must be exact). Each result then says `match`: exact or approximate.

Not paginated.

tools.name: list_municipalities

The municipalities (or alcaldías) of a state with their keys, for a municipality selector or

All municipalities of the state (not paginated; the largest state has 570).

q.description: Text to search, ignoring case and accents (2 to 100 characters, up to 12 words).

tools.name: list_municipality_settlements

Settlements of a municipality.

Every settlement of a municipality; for example, to load the colonias of a municipality into

Ordered by postal code and name. Paginated like /v1/settlements.

**Plan:** every plan.

Returns one page. If `next_cursor` is not null and the user needs more results, call again with `cursor` set to it; never walk every page to copy the catalog.

q.description: Text to search, ignoring case and accents (2 to 100 characters, up to 12 words).

zone.description: Zone. The catalog values (urbano, semiurbano) are also accepted.

limit.description: Page size (1–500, default 50). There is no "unlimited" value: to get every result, follow `next_cursor` until it is null.

cursor.description: Opaque value of `next_cursor` from the previous page, sent as is. Only valid for the data version that issued it (otherwise 400 /errors/cursor-expired).

tools.name: list_settlement_types
tools.description:
Settlement types.

The settlement types that SEPOMEX uses, to filter searches by `type`.

Colonia, Fraccionamiento, Ranchería, Barrio, Pueblo, Ejido, etc. (24 types). Not paginated.

**Plan:** every plan.

tools.name: list_changes
tools.description:
Changes since a data version.

What changed in the catalog since the version you have, so you update only that in your own
database instead of looking everything up again.

Changes published after the data version `since`, oldest first (by version; within a version,
SEPOMEX postal codes, SEPOMEX settlements, SAT postal codes and SAT settlements, each by key).
Store the `data_version` you have, call this endpoint with it, apply the changes and store the
new `data_version`. Paginated: follow `next_cursor`. An empty `data` with `next_cursor: null`
means you are up to date. If you only keep one of the catalogs, skip the entities of the other
(`entity`).

**Plan:** Business and Enterprise.

Returns one page. If `next_cursor` is not null and the user needs more results, call again with `cursor` set to it; never walk every page to copy the catalog.

since.description: Data version you already have (the `data_version` of a previous response). Must be `history_since` or later; otherwise 400 /errors/unknown-version.

limit.description: Page size (1–500, default 50). There is no "unlimited" value: to get every result, follow `next_cursor` until it is null.

cursor.description: Opaque value of `next_cursor` from the previous page, sent as is. Only valid for the data version that issued it (otherwise 400 /errors/cursor-expired).

tools.name: get_sat_postal_code
tools.description:
SAT data of a postal code (CFDI 4.0).

Everything the SAT catalogs say about a postal code: the keys for CFDI 4.0 and its complements, like Carta Porte (state, municipality, locality and settlements), the border region incentive with the validity of its decree, and the time zone as the SAT publishes it and the actual one (`iana`).

Also says which SEPOMEX settlements have no SAT key (`settlements_missing_in_sat`). A suggested counterpart (`sat_candidate`, `sepomex_candidate`) is never the key: confirm it. Works for postal codes that are only in one of the catalogs (`in_sat`, `in_sepomex`).

With `as_of` (a past date, from `sat_history_since` in /v1/meta), what the SAT catalog said that day: for example, on the date of an invoice you are replacing or reviewing.

**Plan:** paid plans (Basic and higher); the demo postal codes on every plan.

The full description and every response field: call get_colonix_guide with topic `get_sat_postal_code`.

as_of.description: Date (YYYY-MM-DD) to get what the SAT catalog said that day, from `sat_history_since` (see /v1/meta) to today in Mexico City.

annotations.title: SAT data of a postal code (CFDI 4.0)

tools.name: list_sat_discrepancies
tools.description:
Differences between the SAT and SEPOMEX catalogs.

Where the SAT and SEPOMEX catalogs disagree: postal codes or settlements that exist in one
and not in the other. Useful to find the addresses that will cause trouble when invoicing.

Ordered by postal code. A settlement matches when the postal code is the same and the name is
the same or equivalent (the rules of the validation: case, accents, common abbreviations, the
settlement type at the beginning, spaces and articles); those are not differences. When the
names do not match but are probably the same place, `possible_match` suggests the counterpart
in the other catalog; it stays in the list until you confirm it. Paginated: follow
`next_cursor`.

For invoicing, what matters is `missing_in=sat`: a postal code that SEPOMEX has and the SAT
does not is rejected in a CFDI, and a settlement without a SAT counterpart has no `c_Colonia`
key for Carta Porte or Comercio Exterior. Almost all postal-code differences go the other way
(`missing_in=sepomex`): codes that only the SAT lists, which are valid in a CFDI.

**Plan:** Business and Enterprise.

Returns one page. If `next_cursor` is not null and the user needs more results, call again with `cursor` set to it; never walk every page to copy the catalog.

missing_in.description: Only items missing in this catalog (default both).

limit.description: Page size (1–500, default 50). There is no "unlimited" value: to get every result, follow `next_cursor` until it is null.

cursor.description: Opaque value of `next_cursor` from the previous page, sent as is. Only valid for the data version that issued it (otherwise 400 /errors/cursor-expired).

annotations.title: Differences between the SAT and SEPOMEX catalogs

tools.name: reverse_geocode
tools.description:
Postal code at a point.

The postal code at a point on the map; for example, from your user's location or from a
delivery.

The postal code whose area contains the point. The areas cover Mexico's land territory,
including about 4,500 rural postal codes that have no settlements in the SEPOMEX catalog
(`in_sepomex_catalog: false`). Areas are simplified to about 10 m: a point right on the boundary
may return the neighbor. A point outside every area returns 404 `/errors/location-not-covered`.
The 537 postal codes without an area of their own (located by `locality_centroid` or
`municipality_centroid`) never come back here: their reference point falls inside another
postal code's area.

**Plan:** paid plans (Basic and higher).

lat.description: Latitude in decimal degrees (WGS84), up to 20 decimals (as a GPS or a browser gives it); rounded to 6 (about 10 cm).

lon.description: Longitude in decimal degrees (WGS84), up to 20 decimals (as a GPS or a browser gives it); rounded to 6 (about 10 cm).

tools.name: find_nearby_postal_codes
tools.description:
Postal codes near a point.

The postal codes around a point, nearest first; for example, to check delivery coverage around
a store.

Postal codes whose reference location is within `radius_km` of the point. The distance is
measured to the reference location, not to the edge of the area. Only postal codes with
`postal_code_polygon` or `locality_centroid` precision are considered. Not paginated.

**Plan:** paid plans (Basic and higher).

lat.description: Latitude in decimal degrees (WGS84), up to 20 decimals (as a GPS or a browser gives it); rounded to 6 (about 10 cm).

lon.description: Longitude in decimal degrees (WGS84), up to 20 decimals (as a GPS or a browser gives it); rounded to 6 (about 10 cm).

radius_km.description: Search radius in kilometers (greater than 0, at most 50, up to 3 decimals).

tools.name: get_data_info
tools.description:
Data version, source and totals.

The current data version, the date of each source and the catalog totals. Use it to check
whether there is a new version before updating your copy.

**Plan:** every plan.

tools.name: get_colonix_guide
tools.description:
Explains Colonix without calling the API: free, needs no API key and does not count toward the quota.

Without `topic`, lists the topics. With a guide topic, returns that documentation guide in Markdown (the guides are in Spanish), with real examples. With the name of a tool, returns every field of that tool's response with its type and meaning.

Use it before explaining a result whose meaning is not obvious, for example: `similarity` (how alike two names are, not a probability), `same_key` (extra evidence, not proof), the `status` of each attribute with include=cfdi (`omit` is Colonix's reading of the SAT rules, not a SAT text), what `as_of` answers, or an error type.

topic.description: A guide (cfdi, matching, sat-sepomex-cases, as-of, ...) or the name of a tool to get its response fields. Omit it to list the topics.

instructions: Colonix answers questions about Mexican postal codes (códigos postales) and their settlements (colonias, fraccionamientos, barrios...) from the official SEPOMEX catalog, cross-referenced with the SAT catalogs for CFDI 4.0. Start with get_postal_code for a 5-digit postal code (keep leading zeros: 06700); validate_postal_code_settlement checks that a colonia belongs to a postal code (include cfdi returns the Domicilio keys for Carta Porte and Comercio Exterior); search_settlements (fuzzy=true tolerates typos) or autocomplete_settlements when you only have a name. State and municipality keys are INEGI keys (list_states, list_municipalities). Every call counts toward the user's monthly quota (batch_get_postal_codes counts one per postal code): avoid unnecessary calls and never page through results to copy the catalog. Some tools need a paid plan: 403 /errors/plan-not-allowed means the user's plan does not include it (plans: https://silgaru.mx/colonix/docs/planes/). get_colonix_guide is free (no API call, no quota): before explaining what a field of a response means (for example similarity, same_key, the cfdi status values or as_of) or an error, read its fields (topic: the tool name) or the related guide instead of guessing.
